title.narrative: REPAM - Ecclesial Panamazonian network - Human Rights Training School and Advocacy

description.narrative:
This project continues CAFOD's assistance to the Ecclesial Pan Amazonian Network (REPAM) in its work to support indigenous peoples, rural communities and missionaries and church's staff working in the wide Amazon region to promote and protect their human rights. These communities have been severely impacted by the advance of mining, large infrastructure projects and climate change in the Amazon region. It aims to enhance the action of the Catholic Church in the region, through establishing a regional Human Rights training school to train community leaders, missionaries and pastoral workers to protect the human right of the local populations including their livelihoods and the common good. It will achieve this through: • setting up the HR training school, definition of school's structure, training methodology, curriculum, selection of trainers, application and selection systems, carrying out training and after course accompaniment. • to promote HR advocacy - selection of emblematic cases from course's participants, preparation of cases, visibility and communication, presenting and following up cases presented to Inter American Human Rights court and local courts.
This approval is aligned with CAFOD's strategic priorities 1.3 and 1.1 to improve governance and human rights issues in the global South due to the interventions of the Catholic Church and Laudato Si influences and informs development and programmes.
